We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON tree: root molecule, then reaction nodes each with template_id, children being precursor molecules (type mol). The route must have at least 5 reactions, i.e., 5 levels? The order of templates must be applied sequentially from target to precursors. So first apply template 29646 to target, get precursors. Then for each precursor (maybe one), apply template 1914389, etc.

We need to find applicable precursors using apply_template tool. We already attempted applying 29646 to target and got three possible outcomes (tuples). The result was:

"(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C',))"

So three possible retrosynthetic splits. Need to choose one that can continue through the remaining templates.

We need to apply 1914389 next. Let's test each candidate.

First candidate: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". Apply 1914389 gave earlier result: we applied to that and got two products: ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'). So that splits into two precursors: one is similar but with CC=O (aldehyde) and the other is an ester with phosphonate? Actually second is CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC.

Thus after 1914389 we have two molecules. Next template 1914390 must be applied to each? The order says use templates in this order, but we have 5 reactions total. Likely each reaction step applies to a single molecule, but we can have branching. The route must have at least 5 reactions total, maybe linear chain of 5 steps. Could choose a path where each step yields a single precursor (i.e., unimolecular). The first template gave three possible splits; maybe choose the third which is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C". That's a simpler molecule lacking protecting groups. Let's test applying 1914389 to that; earlier we tried and got no result. So not good.

Second candidate: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Apply 1914389 gave no result.

Thus only first candidate works for 1914389.

Now apply 1914390 to each of the two precursors from step 2.

We already applied 1914390 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and got result: ('CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1',). That's a single product (precursor). Good.

Now apply 1914390 to the second precursor "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". That gave no result earlier.

Thus we may need to treat the route as branching: after step 2 we have two molecules; we apply 1914390 only to the first, and maybe the second will be a final commercial building block (no further steps). But we still need to apply templates 149040 and 1914391 later. The order must be used; maybe we apply 149040 to the product from 1914390 (the aldehyde derivative). Let's test applying 149040 to "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". Earlier we attempted and got empty result. So maybe need to apply 149040 to a different intermediate.

Alternatively, maybe we should choose a different path: after 1914389, we could apply 1914390 to the second precursor (phosphonate) but it didn't work. Maybe we need to apply 149040 to the second precursor? The order is fixed, but maybe we can apply 149040 to the second precursor after 1914390 step on the first? The order says use templates in this order, but not necessarily each step must be applied to each branch; we can apply next template to any molecule that still needs disconnection. So after step 2 we have two molecules; we apply 1914390 to the first (makes new precursor). Then we still have the second unchanged; next template 149040 could be applied to either of the remaining molecules that are suitable. Let's test applying 149040 to the second precursor "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". It gave empty earlier. So not.

Maybe we need to apply 149040 to the product from 1914390 (the cyclic ester). It gave empty earlier. So maybe we need to choose a different initial split from 29646 that leads to a chain of 5 steps.

Let's examine other splits.

Second split from 29646: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Apply 1914389 gave no result. So not.

Third split: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C". Apply 1914389 gave no result. So only first split works.

Thus we must work with that.

Now after 1914390 we have product A: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". Also we still have the phosphonate B: "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Need to apply 149040 next. Let's test applying 149040 to product A again maybe with different orientation? Already empty. Could apply to B? empty.

Maybe we need to apply 149040 to a different intermediate earlier. Perhaps we should apply 149040 to the product of 1914389 before 1914390? Let's test applying 149040 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". That is the precursor before 1914390. We attempted earlier and got empty.

Maybe 149040 is a deprotection of silyl group? Let's inspect its SMARTS: from get_template, retro_smarts_template: '[C:2]-[Si;H0;D4;+0:1](-[C;D1;H3:3])(-[C;D1;H3:4])-[O;H0;D2;+0:6]-[C:5]>>F-C(-F)(-F)-S(=O)(=O)-O-[Si;H0;D4;+0:1](-[C:2])(-[C;D1;H3:3])-[C;D1;H3:4].[C:5]-[OH;D1;+0:6]'

So it's a silyl protecting group removal with fluorosulfonyl? Actually it replaces Si group with something else. The forward reaction attaches a silyl group to an alcohol? The retro removes silyl and yields a fluorosulfonyl group? Not sure.

Our molecule has a silyl group attached to O: "...CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". So applying 149040 should break Si-O bond and produce something else (maybe a fluorosulfonyl group). But our earlier attempts gave product(s) where the silyl group is removed and replaced with something else: result from applying 149040 to the original target gave empty. But applying to the first split gave result: ("C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO", "CC(C)(C)[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F") So it splits into two fragments: the deprotected molecule (without silyl) and a silyl-sulfonyl fragment. That seems promising. That was applying 149040 to the original target? Actually we applied to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". That gave two fragments: deprotected version (no Si) and a silyl-sulfonyl fragment.

Thus maybe the correct order: after 1914389 we have that silyl-protected molecule; then 149040 removes the silyl group, giving the deprotected target (which is close to original but without silyl). Then 1914391 could be applied to something else? Let's test applying 1914391 to the deprotected molecule "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". Apply 1914391.
